owner_sentences.sentence: Trước hết xác minh hợp đồng gọi đồng thời; lựa chọn RLock hay cách sửa khác phải dựa trên đường gọi thực tế.
owner_sentences.evidence: Every .release() caller in aisef2/ re-grepped and its thread read (client.py:218, adapters.py:291, test_execution.py:469, the four probes, StoryScope._release worker, Ranged, ToolCall.finish, RunScope.interrupt, the single SIGINT handler run_scope.py:254 that only sets a flag, mutation.py:1556/1583 sequential twice, no fork/multiprocessing/atexit/__del__ in aisef2): no product path overlaps two releases of one range; two by-design tests and a constructed abandoned-worker case do. This is a reading, not a measurement. The mechanism is argued from the contract and the RLock/Lock/swallow alternatives were re-applied to BASE and measured (RLock 7 of 32 fail, Lock 8, swallow 18).

owner_sentences.sentence: Có test tái hiện bằng điều phối luồng có kiểm soát, kiểm tra tính idempotent, quyền sở hữu tiến trình và tránh deadlock.
owner_sentences.evidence: At the implementer's head the 25 tests passed three wrong implementations: a claim with no lock (and no _mx attribute), a claim with a lock around read and write separately (TOCTOU), and a waiter that returns once the leader is `disposing` (before the reap, pipe close and escapee check). RealRange (barrier aligned) saw the unlocked claim 0 times in 100 runs. 7 tests added; each fails those variants deterministically and passes the correct code 40/40.

owner_sentences.sentence: Không chỉ lặp test nhiều lần rồi kết luận hết lỗi.
owner_sentences.evidence: The proof is the deterministic choreography (fake backend, thread parking); loops are labelled a supplement, and the guest loop that does not discriminate is said so. One test (ClaimAndWait claim test) uses a bounded wait (CLAIM_PROBE_S = 1 s) whose expiry is the expected outcome in a correct run; it can not fail a correct implementation.

defects_found.what: TEST GAP: the atomicity of the claim across threads is not tested. A claim with no lock (no _mx attribute: the only test that looks for _mx skips) and a claim in two critical sections both pass all 25 tests; RealRange saw the unlocked claim 0/100.

TEST GAP: nothing holds a second caller while the leader is past the ladder. A waiter that returns when `disposing` is set (before reap, pipe close, escapee check) passes all 25 (by the 20 ms poll granularity) and re-creates the silent leak for that waiter.

UNSTABLE KILL: release mutant [17] (L457 'not' removed: a waiter that spins) was INFRA in one full run and in 1 of 3 isolated runs; killed by a different test each time (only a rare hang window made the file fail). It would have been a coin flip in the lead's re-measurement.

TEST GAP (pre-existing): deleting the second look at escapees in _release (Linux orphan re-parented to the anchor) is caught by neither the new file nor tests/v2/p4/test_process_range.py, on the host or in the guest.
DOC: validation importer count (15 not 16); ProcessRange.__init__ missing from the registration list; the asynchronous-exception window mis-stated; 'real' labels for the io test and the guest run.

DESIGN (owner, not changed): the outcome a caller gets from a concurrent release depends on whether it arrived during the release (RangeEscaped) or after it (None). In the two by-design tests the stop thread's exception is read by nobody, so whether the probe's own finally sees a leak depends on a microsecond window. No product path has such a pair.
RESIDUAL: a leader that dies of a non-Residual after the reap (e.g. process_table() failing in the escapee check) hands its waiters None: the escapee check did not complete for anyone.

STYLE (rule 6): three tests assert whole messages of RangeNotEmpty/RangeEscaped (the text is old, moved byte for byte; the assertion pins that). One design-bound assertion (polling) rejects a correct blocking-lock implementation (RLock/Lock alternatives fail AbandonedWorker for that reason as well).

remaining_risks: Windows nothing run; Python 3.11/3.13 not run (3.12.14, 3.14.7, 3.14.8 run).
A real asynchronous signal is not exercised: the 'handler' is a call from inside a backend operation / the claim / the poll on the same thread.
ClaimAndWait claim test waits on a bounded Event (1 s) whose expiry is the expected outcome; the only wall-clock element of the file.
Two tests are design-bound to this mechanism (claim lock attribute _mx; polling by the module's time.sleep): a different correct mechanism needs them updated.
Waiters inherit the leader's bound; with wait_s=None a waiter waits as long as the leader would have.
Outcome of a concurrent release depends on arrival time (D1).
A flight can be stranded by an asynchronous exception inside the finally before done = True (two bytecodes); not closed.
Sealed records bound to aisef2/ or process_range.py are stale by construction: lead regenerates.
decisions_needed: D1 (owner): should a range that completed a release in RangeEscaped re-raise it to every later caller? Today only a caller that arrived DURING the release gets it; after it ends the caller gets None and a StoryScope records RELEASED (so worktree/scratch are not held back, §17.1). Option (ii) keeps the Residual on the range; RangeNotEmpty keeps re-running the ladder (mutation.py:1583).
D2 (owner): Windows failed adopt: _Job.abort does not signal an anchor that never joined the job, so _abort waits on it (from reading; not run).
D3 (owner): p4.test_interruption RealSignals SIGINT_mid_story hung once in 150 runs on BASE (pre-existing, unexplained).

Lead: register ProcessRange._ladder, ProcessRange._release, _Flight.__init__ (new) and ProcessRange.release, ProcessRange.__init__ (changed) with the kill files above; regenerate the sealed records; accept or reject the 1 s bounded wait of the claim test and the two design-bound assertions; update REPORT.md (Q-RANGE row) and the MUTATION-RUNNER-V2.md paragraph on the intermittent failure.
